en.caption: Gem Stories
rows: One of the party's patrons dies, and the patron's will bequeaths all their wealth to the characters.
The party is hired by a disguised dragon who offers them part of its hoard as payment.
A character falls through a crevice and discovers a massive deposit of glittering ore.
The party finds a map in an old bottle that leads to a buried treasure chest filled with ancient coins.
The local merchants' guild, enamored with the party's exploits, offers to sponsor the characters.
The characters are invited to participate in a grand talent competition. Despite the odds, one of the characters wins.

rows: Protect a sanctuary that hides martyrs' remains until the martyrs are called back to life to oppose a world-changing foe.
Gather the lost shards of a dead god's petrified body, and reunite them on the altar in the medusa's lair.
Maintain a planar crossing from which great power flows while also curtailing the effects of that power as it infuses the world.
Seek out a new generation of champions, and train them to fight in a war.
Tend a sacred beacon fed by the Outer Planes, sending embers of that beacon to the corners of the world to maintain a divine shroud.
Watch the entrance to a slumbering titan's tomb for any sign the titan might awaken, and repel the forces that seek to break the tomb's seal.

en.caption: Seelie Market Introductions
rows: A strange trail of toadstools leads off the beaten path into the nearby woods.
A pixie beckons you to follow her, promising you a sight beyond your wildest dreams.
A man stumbles from the forest. He doesn't speak, but his arms are full of delicious-looking fruit.
The party hears chattering voices and the music of panpipes coming from a secluded area.
In the distance, the party sees a descending dragon pulling a caravan of wagons.
A dragon's gentle voice calls out to the characters in their dreams, giving them directions to the market but no further details.

en.caption: Deck of Wild Cards
rows: The card explodes in a burst of fire. The target and each creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 2d8} fire damage.

The card shoots streaks of lightning. The target must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the blinded condition until the end of your next turn, and each creature within 10 feet of the target takes {@damage 1d6} lightning damage.

The card covers the target in a thick layer of ice. The target takes {@damage 1d10} cold damage and must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or have the restrained condition until the end of your next turn.

The card unleashes a sharp, concussive blast. The target and each creature within 5 feet of it take {@damage 1d6} force damage and must succeed on a {@dc 15} Strength saving throw or have the prone condition.

en.caption: Ruin Encounters
rows: Animals—such as a {@creature brown bear}, {@creature giant owl}, or pack of {@dice 2d6} {@creature Wolf||wolves}—attack, made vicious by the effect of Baphomet's temple deep under the hill.
{@dice 2d4} {@creature Minotaur Archaeologist|BMT|minotaur archaeologists} explore the hill, looking for artifacts and places to dig.

{@dice 1d6} {@creature Minotaur Infiltrator|BMT|minotaur infiltrators} are performing a bloody rite to Baphomet; if there are six, one is their leader, {@creature Brusipha|BMT} (both stat blocks appear in this chapter). If discovered, the minotaurs attack to conceal their activity from outsiders.

{@dice 1d3} {@creature Displacer Beast||displacer beasts}, pets of the green hags, are on the prowl; alternatively, use {@creature Yeth Hound|MPMM|yeth hounds} from {@book Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse|MPMM}.

A plaintive howl echoes over the hill. Characters who succeed on a {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check identify the source as the collapsed bell tower in the Feygrove, where a young {@creature displacer beast} is trapped.

A {@creature green hag} from the coven hidden in the Feygrove is on a mysterious errand. If she detects the adventurers before they spot her, the hag uses Illusory Appearance to conceal herself as a dryad and invites the characters to the Feygrove, then returns to her coven and sets a trap for the characters.

Vegetation on the hillside has grown into a hedge maze due to the magical influence of Baphomet's temple. Navigating the maze requires 1 hour and a successful {@dc 18} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check.
Mekkalath's presence prompts a fiery eruption. Creatures in a 5-foot-radius, 20-foot-high cylinder must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or take 17 ({@dice 5d6}) fire damage.
{@dice 1d3} {@creature Fire Elemental||fire elementals} drawn from the Elemental Plane of Fire by Mekkalath's aura wander the hill.

Spiders from the Feygrove are on the prowl; they include {@dice 2d4} {@creature Giant Spider||giant spiders} plus either {@dice 1d3} {@creature Phase Spider||phase spiders} or 1 {@creature ruin spider|BMT}.
A lone {@creature githyanki warrior} hunts for tonight's meal.
A {@creature red slaad}, dropped here by the comet that recently overflew the site, searches the hill for any way to lift the wards around the watchtower.
en.name: Ruin Encounters

en.caption: Zodiac Phenomena
rows: Skull. The unliving surge with renewed zeal. Undead in the region gain 13 ({@dice 3d8}) {@book temporary hit points|PHB|9|Temporary Hit Points} daily at dusk.
Balance. Each creature in the region intuitively knows the immunities, resistances, and vulnerabilities of any creature it sees in the region.
Sage. Emotions are muted in the region, but minds open to new ideas. Creatures in the region have advantage on Charisma checks made to improve the attitude of other creatures in the region.
Throne. The resolve of the law-abiding is bolstered, while rebels are emboldened to passionately pursue their causes. Creatures in the region are immune to the {@condition frightened} condition.
Key. A creature can unlock an object in this region simply by touching it, even if the lock is magical.

Flames. Emotions in the region become more intense. Whenever a creature in the region tries to alter the attitude of another, a failed Charisma check always results in the latter creature turning hostile if it wasn't hostile already.

Knight. Spectral knights routinely fly across the sky. Whenever the characters are outdoors and become embroiled in combat in the region, one or more knights descend from the sky to help them, provided none of the characters is evil. Each round on initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the knights deal 9 ({@dice 2d8}) force damage to each of the characters' enemies. After the battle, the knights bow, then disappear.

Euryale. Natural vegetation in the region grows poisonous thorns. A creature that enters or ends its turn in {@book difficult terrain|PHB|8|Difficult Terrain} caused by this vegetation must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or take 7 ({@dice 2d6}) poison damage. If this damage reduces a creature to 0 hit points, the creature instead has 1 hit point and has the {@condition petrified} condition until that condition is removed by the {@spell Greater Restoration} spell or similar magic.
Rogue. Sneaks find their efforts easier in the region. Creatures in the region make Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks with advantage.

Gem. At midnight on a clear night, the stars appear to multiply tenfold, then rain down to the ground as minuscule silver meteorites. In all, 100 gp worth of silver falls harmlessly from the sky, scattered throughout the region.
Talons. Some magic is suppressed in the region. Common magic items, cantrips, and 1st-level spells don't function within this area.

Jester. Misfortune besets people in the region. Whenever a Humanoid in the region makes an ability check or an attack roll and rolls a 1 on the {@dice d20}, it has the {@condition incapacitated} condition until the end of its next turn, as it is magically overcome with laughter.
en.name: Zodiac Phenomena

Rogue. Sneaks find their efforts easier in the region. Creatures in the region make Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks with advantage.

Gem. At midnight on a clear night, the stars appear to multiply tenfold, then rain down to the ground as minuscule silver meteorites. In all, 100 gp worth of silver falls harmlessly from the sky, scattered throughout the region.
Talons. Some magic is suppressed in the region. Common magic items, cantrips, and 1st-level spells don't function within this area.

Jester. Misfortune besets people in the region. Whenever a Humanoid in the region makes an ability check or an attack roll and rolls a 1 on the {@dice d20}, it has the {@condition incapacitated} condition until the end of its next turn, as it is magically overcome with laughter.

cells: Skull. The unliving surge with renewed zeal. Undead in the region gain 13 ({@dice 3d8}) {@book temporary hit points|PHB|9|Temporary Hit Points} daily at dusk.
Balance. Each creature in the region intuitively knows the immunities, resistances, and vulnerabilities of any creature it sees in the region.
Sage. Emotions are muted in the region, but minds open to new ideas. Creatures in the region have advantage on Charisma checks made to improve the attitude of other creatures in the region.
Throne. The resolve of the law-abiding is bolstered, while rebels are emboldened to passionately pursue their causes. Creatures in the region are immune to the {@condition frightened} condition.
Key. A creature can unlock an object in this region simply by touching it, even if the lock is magical.

Flames. Emotions in the region become more intense. Whenever a creature in the region tries to alter the attitude of another, a failed Charisma check always results in the latter creature turning hostile if it wasn't hostile already.

Knight. Spectral knights routinely fly across the sky. en.caption: Fortunes
rows: "Carry a lit flame with you at all times. You will be rewarded with wondrous treasure."
"You are fated to witness a terrible catastrophe. Take solace in knowing there is nothing you can do to stop it."
"Someone who seems helpless will call for your aid. Do not trust them."
"A dream will bring answers to the questions you seek."
"Someone will offer you their services in a time of great need. Trust them."
"A foe is hunting you. They seek vengeance and shall arrive soon."
"You will soon lose something you hold dear."
"Give advice freely and often. It will save another's life in the near future, earning you their loyalty."
"Great responsibility shall be thrust upon you. Only you will know if you are ready."

en.caption: Marks of the Donjon
rows: The character's vision is limited to a 5-foot-wide line pointing in a single direction.
The character gets nauseous near windows or doorways. If the character moves through such a threshold, the character has disadvantage on saving throws for 1 minute.
The character is plagued by nightmares of metal constructs.
The character is disoriented by wide-open spaces and has no sense of direction outdoors.
While in sunlight, the character has disadvantage on attack rolls.

en.caption: Sage Destinies
rows: You were once a member of an order dedicated to keeping magical artifacts out of the hands of those who would abuse their power.
A seer predicted you're destined for immense power. Do you seek this power or reject it?
Your dreams include visions of an imprisoned extraplanar entity.
You wish to learn powerful magic to protect your loved ones from harm.
Your magical studies are driven by a desire to manipulate reality.
Your magical ability stems from a gamble you made with a Fiend—though you're not sure if you won or lost.
You use your arcane prowess to con unsuspecting individuals.
You carry a seemingly ordinary item stolen from a powerful archmage, and it causes inexplicable things to happen around you.
You come from a long tradition of wild mages, even if your own powers are different.
Your spellbook manifests as a deck of cards.
Your family of renowned warriors judges you on your martial talents (or lack thereof).
A loved one is cursed, and you're determined to break that curse.
You live for the pursuit of arcane secrets and lost legends.
Someone you trust is actually a monster, such as a dragon or a hag, in disguise.
A fortune teller warned that you're destined to cause great destruction, which you're trying to avoid.
You use a divinatory card spread to decide which spells to prepare each day.
You seek a way to cheat death.
Your spells and magical abilities take on the appearance of playing cards.
Agents of the Solar Bastion (see {@area chapter 10|148|x}) once saved your life.
You seek to reclaim a stolen magical artifact.
You began your arcane scholarship as an apprentice to a court magician.
You've glimpsed another plane of existence, but no one believes you. You strive to prove them wrong.

en.caption: Solar Bastion Quests
rows: Aid and Counsel. Your contact has learned another group of adventurers has discovered a {@item Deck of Many Things}. Find them before they draw from it, and warn them of its dangers—or help them get out of the mess their draws bring upon them.
Research. A rare tome said to describe early encounters with Decks of Many Things is thought to lie in the hoard of a dragon. Retrieve it!
Track Rifflers. {@creature Riffler|BMT|Rifflers} have been active in a remote countryside. Find out if they have a {@item Deck of Many Things}, and ensure they don't give it to a hapless mortal.

Stay Ahead of the Grim Harrow. Riders of the Grim Harrow (see {@area chapter 19|2d8|x}) are terrorizing a village as they search for a {@item Deck of Many Things}. Figure out where they're going, and get there before they do!

Find {@creature Euryale|BMT}. Rumors of a reclusive medusa are spreading through a city. There's a slim chance the medusa could be {@creature Euryale|BMT}, who could lead the knights to {@creature Asteria|BMT}. Determine the medusa's identity and secretly follow her trail, if any, to {@creature Asteria|BMT}.

Prevent Misuse. A {@creature Hierophant of the Comet|BMT|hierophant} of the Heralds of the Comet (see {@area chapter 12|198|x}) has acquired a few cards from the original {@item Deck of Many Things}. Ensure the complete artifact doesn't fall into her hands.
Combat a Curse. After plundering a dragon's hoard, adventurers attract constant ill luck. Make sure the treasure isn't cursed; if it is, ensure they aren't spreading the curse as they spend the gold.

Contain an Evil Artifact. The blights and ruination befalling a region suggest someone there is casting spells from the {@item Book of Vile Darkness} or perhaps wielding the {@item Wand of Orcus}. Do whatever is necessary to stop this person, and bring the evil artifact back to Hilarion so it can be contained.

en.caption: Solar Bastion Contact
rows: Restless Retiree. Gundra, an ancient dwarf, served the Solar Bastion in the field for over a century before retiring. She lives in the Solar Bastion now and relentlessly drills the knights she trains. She clearly misses working in the field.
Grumpy Veteran. Howart, an older human, has mentored many young adventurers, but most were smart enough to listen to his advice... unlike you lot, who seem to think you know everything.
Busy Supervisor. Theira, a frazzled elf, has so many irons in the fire, so many projects to keep track of! Of course you're not imposing, she says, but can you get quickly to the point, please?

Distracted Researcher. Haddick, a middle-aged halfling, spends most of her time in the Library Tower at the Solar Bastion. Even when she's not at the library, or when she's talking to you, it's pretty clear that her mind is still there, focused on her latest subject of research.

Lonely Knight. Jared, a human knight of the Solar Bastion with a distinguished career, has traveled the multiverse alone so long he's become isolated and unsure of himself in social situations. He wants to help but needs encouragement to regain his naturally friendly demeanor.
Hilarion. The solar speaks to you directly, via the {@spell Sending} spell or after summoning you to the Solar Bastion.

en.caption: Fey Fruit Effects
rows: Every 10 minutes, the creature must eat another fey fruit or make a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw, gaining 1 level of {@condition exhaustion} on a failed save. Magic that ends the {@condition charmed} condition cures the cravings, which otherwise end after 1 hour.
The creature turns a sickly green and has the {@condition poisoned} condition for 1 hour.
The creature can't deliberately lie for 24 hours.
The creature can't understand any language for the next 8 hours.
The creature turns into a {@creature Faerie Dragon (Violet)||faerie dragon}, as if by a {@spell True Polymorph} spell that has a duration of 24 hours.
Regenerative bark covers the creature's skin, granting the effects of a {@spell Barkskin} spell for 24 hours.
The creature and anything it is wearing or carrying become {@condition invisible} for 24 hours. This invisibility ends early immediately after the creature attacks or casts a spell.
The creature gains the benefits of a {@spell Speak with Animals} spell for 8 hours.
The creature gains {@dice 4d4 + 4} {@book temporary hit points|PHB|9|Temporary Hit Points}.
The creature sprouts dragonfly-like wings, gaining a flying speed of 30 feet for 1 hour.

en.caption: Telescope Travel Mishaps
rows: The travelers appear adrift in the Astral Sea.
The travelers appear on a different plane of existence, determined randomly or chosen by the DM.

Excess cosmic energy overloads the telescope, causing it to explode. Each creature within 60 feet of the telescope takes {@dice 8d6} necrotic damage. Any Humanoid who survives this damage is transformed into a different kind of creature, as if it had been subject to the {@spell Reincarnate} spell.
A creature from the Astral Sea (such as a {@creature githyanki knight}) appears within 60 feet of the telescope. The DM decides its attitude.
The travelers appear on a different planet or celestial body in the Wildspace system nearest to their target destination.
The travelers arrive at their intended destination, but they each appear coated in harmless slime.

en.caption: Cair Ophidian Flowers
rows: Nonmagical Flower. This bloom has no magical properties but is very pretty.

Swift Lily. This flower crackles with energy. As a bonus action, you can crush the flower to increase your speed by 30 feet until the start of your next turn. The flower is then destroyed. The flower loses its magic {@dice 1d6} days after being plucked.

Drowsing Lavender. This stalk of purple blooms glows faintly. As an action, you can wave it at a creature within your reach. The creature must succeed on a {@dc 17} Wisdom saving throw or have the {@condition unconscious} condition until the start of your next turn. Once used this way, the flower is destroyed. The flower loses its magic {@dice 1d8} days after being plucked.

Iron Peony. This flower's petals are silver-tipped. As a bonus action, you can crush the flower to gain resistance to all damage until the start of your next turn. The flower is then destroyed. This flower loses its magic {@dice 1d12} days after being plucked.

Wishing Lion. This flower appears as a dandelion with a tiny lion head embedded in the fluff. As an action, you can blow on the fluff and cast the {@spell Wish} spell. The flower is then destroyed. This flower retains its magic until the spell is cast.

Drowsing Lavender. This stalk of purple blooms glows faintly. As an action, you can wave it at a creature within your reach. The creature must succeed on a {@dc 17} Wisdom saving throw or have the {@condition unconscious} condition until the start of your next turn. Once used this way, the flower is destroyed. The flower loses its magic {@dice 1d8} days after being plucked.

Iron Peony. This flower's petals are silver-tipped. As a bonus action, you can crush the flower to gain resistance to all damage until the start of your next turn. The flower is then destroyed. This flower loses its magic {@dice 1d12} days after being plucked.

Wishing Lion. This flower appears as a dandelion with a tiny lion head embedded in the fluff. As an action, you can blow on the fluff and cast the {@spell Wish} spell. The flower is then destroyed. This flower retains its magic until the spell is cast.
